aboutPage.title: About CBSoft
aboutPage.p1: The Brazilian Conference on Software: Theory and Practice (CBSoft) is held annually by the Brazilian Computer Society (SBC) to promote the exchange of experience among researchers and practitioners from academia and industry on research, trends and innovations, both theoretical and practical, in software. Held since 2010, CBSoft brings together the Brazilian software symposia promoted by SBC and has become one of the main events of the Brazilian Computing research community.
aboutPage.p2: In 2027, the 18th edition of CBSoft will be held in person in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, from September 27 to October 1, bringing together four symposia held annually by the Brazilian software community:
aboutPage.metaDescription: About CBSoft, the Brazilian Conference on Software: Theory and Practice, its symposia and the activities of the 2027 edition in Belo Horizonte.
aboutPage.program: The program includes technical sessions with paper presentations, keynotes by researchers from Brazil and abroad, panel discussions, workshops and tool demonstrations. These activities foster the dissemination of knowledge and the discussion of research, development and innovation in software.

visualIdentity.title: CBSoft 2027 Visual Identity
visualIdentity.photoAlt: The Niemeyer Building in Belo Horizonte, with its curved façade and flowering trees in the foreground
visualIdentity.photoCaption: Niemeyer Building, Oscar Niemeyer, 1954, Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais
visualIdentity.logoAlt: Official CBSOFT'27 logo — Brazilian Conference on Software, Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais
visualIdentity.conceptP1: The brand’s main visual reference is the Niemeyer Building, designed by Oscar Niemeyer in 1954 and located near Praça da Liberdade, in central Belo Horizonte. Its curved lines express the lightness and fluidity of modernist architecture and recall the mountainous landscape of Minas Gerais.
visualIdentity.conceptP2: This balance between lightness and structure echoes software development, which demands technical rigor as well as creativity and adaptability.

aboutSbc.title: About SBC
aboutSbc.p1: The Brazilian Computer Society (SBC) is a non-profit scientific society, founded in July 1978, that brings together students, professors, professionals, researchers and enthusiasts in Computing from all over the country.
aboutSbc.p2: SBC aims to foster access to information and culture through Computing, promote digital inclusion, encourage research and teaching in Computing in Brazil, and contribute to the education of socially responsible Computing professionals.
aboutSbc.p3: To organize and promote scientific, technical, educational and political activities, actions and events, SBC maintains three types of Thematic Groups (GT): the Major Areas (GA), the Special Committees (CE) and the Interest Groups (GI), which bring together members with common interests in subfields of Computing.
aboutSbc.p4: This is the website of an event promoted by SBC Special Committees (CE), which bring together members who share interests in a given area of Computing. Members in good standing can subscribe to the Special Committees mailing lists for the areas they wish to follow. To join SBC or renew your membership, visit the membership page.

experiencesPage.title: Experiences
experiencesPage.intro: Make the most of CBSoft 2027 to get to know Belo Horizonte, one of Brazil's most welcoming state capitals. The city offers cultural attractions, historic sites, green spaces and nationally renowned food.
experiencesPage.introGuide: Here are some suggestions, grouped by area and interest, so you can enjoy the city beyond the academic programme.

categoryIntros.pampulha: Home to the Pampulha Modern Ensemble, designed by Oscar Niemeyer and listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A good choice for a free afternoon or early evening.
categoryIntros.turismo: Cultural and historic attractions and viewpoints across the city.
categoryIntros.gastronomia: Belo Horizonte is known as Brazil's capital of botecos (neighbourhood bars). Take the chance to try Minas Gerais cooking and the city's main food districts.

conductPage.title: Code of Conduct
conductPage.p1: The open exchange of ideas and the freedom of thought and expression are central to the goals of CBSoft. This requires an environment that recognizes the worth of every person and group, fosters dignity, understanding and mutual respect, and embraces diversity. For these reasons, CBSoft is committed to providing a harassment-free experience for participants, both at the event and on its official communication channels, including social media. The goal is for every participant to feel welcome, included, respected and safe. Hostile or unwelcome behavior, and any speech that intimidates, creates discomfort or interferes with anyone’s participation in the event, will not be tolerated.
conductPage.p2: Unacceptable behavior includes: abusive or degrading language, sustained disruption of a talk, discussion or other activity, discrimination, deliberate intimidation, stalking, harassing photography or recording, inappropriate physical contact, sexual imagery or unwelcome sexual attention.
conductPage.p3: Harassment includes: derogatory comments, writings or actions related to race, color, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, religion, nationality, disability, pregnancy, medical conditions, veteran status or any other status protected by Brazilian law.
conductPage.p4: Anyone who witnesses or is subjected to unacceptable behavior or harassment should report it to a member of the CBSoft 2027 Organizing Committee or to event security. Claims that the behavior was “just a joke” will not be accepted. Anyone who violates these standards may be sanctioned or excluded from the event, without any refund or compensation, at the discretion of the CBSoft 2027 Organizing Committee.

volunteersPage.title: Call for Volunteers
volunteersPage.p1: CBSoft 2027 invites undergraduate and graduate students to apply to serve as volunteers.
volunteersPage.p2: Volunteers play a key role in the success of the event's activities. Volunteering is an excellent opportunity to meet researchers and professionals in Software Engineering.
volunteersPage.p3: Volunteering at CBSoft 2027 is open to students from all over Brazil. We are looking for volunteers to work on site during the event, which will take place in Belo Horizonte.
benefits: A CBSoft 2027 student volunteer T-shirt, plus all the goodies given to participants, lunch on the days you work at the event and coffee breaks throughout the conference.
A great opportunity to meet and talk about research or your interests with researchers and industry professionals.
A chance to build connections with future colleagues in your career.
volunteersPage.preparation: On the day before the event starts: preparation (assembling kits, preparing badges, etc.).
responsibilities: technical support for speakers and participants;
directions to the different event spaces;
support for the event organization team;
contributing to the overall smooth running of the event.
volunteersPage.socialMedia: Some volunteers may take part in the event's social media coverage, producing photos and videos of talks, technical sessions, social activities and other moments of the conference.
requirements: Be enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program during the event.
No previous volunteering experience is required, but we are looking for motivated and committed people.
